text: If the solution curve of the differential equation (2x $-$ $10y^{3})dy +$ ydx = 0, passes through the points (0, 1) and (2, $β$), then $β$ is a root of the equation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(2x-10y^{3})dy+ydx=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}+\left (\frac{2}{y}\right )x=10y^{2}$

$I.F.=e^{\int \frac{2}{y}dy}=e^{2\ln (y)}=y^{2}$

Solution of D.E. is

$\therefore$ $x.\quad y=\int (10y^{2})y^{2}.dy$

$xy^{2}=\frac{10y^{5}}{5}+C\Rightarrow xy^{2}=2y^{5}+C$

It passes through (0, 1) $\to$ 0 = 2 + C $\Rightarrow$ C = $-$2

$\therefore$ Curve is $xy^{2}=2y^{5}-2$

Now, it passes through (2, $β$)

$2β^{2}=2β^{5}-2\Rightarrow β^{5}-β^{2}-1=0$

$\therefore$ $β$ is root of an equation $y^{5}-y^{2}-1=0$

text:
Let [$λ$] be the greatest integer less than or equal to $λ$. The set of all values of $λ$ for which the system of linear equations 
x + y + z = 4, 
3x + 2y + 5z = 3, 
9x + 4y + (28 + [$λ$])z = [$λ$] has a solution is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $k=[λ]$, an integer. The determinant of coefficients is

$D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 5 \\ 9 & 4 & 28+k \end{array}\right |=(36+2k)-(39+3k)+(12-18)=-(k+9)$

If $k\neq -9$, then $D\neq 0$ and the system has a unique solution.

If $k=-9$, the third equation is $9x+4y+19z=-9$. Writing $E_{1}:x+y+z=4$ and $E_{2}:3x+2y+5z=3$, the combination $5E_{2}-6E_{1}$ gives $9x+4y+19z=15-24=-9$, which is exactly the third equation. The system then reduces to the two independent equations $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ and has infinitely many solutions.

So a solution exists for every integer value of $[λ]$, that is, for every real $λ$, and the required set is $\mathrm{ℝ}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: The set of all values of k > $-$1, for which the equation $(3x^{2}+4x+3)^{2}-(k+1)(3x^{2}+4x+3)(3x^{2}+4x+2)+k(3x^{2}+4x+2)^{2}=0$ has real roots, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(3x^{2}+4x+3)^{2}-(k+1)(3x^{2}+4x+3)(3x^{2}+4x+2)+k(3x^{2}+4x+2)^{2}=0$

Let $3x^{2}+4x+3=a$

and $3x^{2}+4x+2=b\Rightarrow b=a-1$

Given equation becomes

$\Rightarrow a^{2}-(k+1)ab+kb^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow a(a-kb)-b(a-kb)=0$

$\Rightarrow (a-kb)(a-b)=0\Rightarrow a=kb$ or a = b (reject) $\because$ a = kb

$\Rightarrow 3x^{2}+4x+3=k(3x^{2}+4x+2)$

$\Rightarrow 3(k-1)x^{2}+4(k-1)x+(2k-3)=0$ for real roots

D $\geq$ 0

$\Rightarrow 16(k-1)^{2}-4(3(k-1))(2k-3)\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow 4(k-1)\{4(k-1)-3(2k-3)\}\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow 4(k-1)\{-2k+5\}\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow -4(k-1)\{2k-5\}\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow (k-1)(2k-5)\leq 0$

 
[IMG]
 

$\therefore$ $k\in \left [1,\frac{5}{2}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $k\neq 1$

$\therefore$ $k\in \left (1,\frac{5}{2}\right ]$

solution.body:

V = l . b . h = (a $-$ 2x)(b $-$ 2x) x

$\Rightarrow$ V(x) = (2x $-$ a)(2x $-$ b) x

$\Rightarrow$ $V(x) = 4x^{3}$ $-$ $2(a + b)x^{2} +$ abx

$\Rightarrow \frac{d}{dx}v(x)=12x^{2}-4(a+b)x+ab$

$\frac{d}{dx}(v(x))=0\Rightarrow 12x^{2}-4(a+b)x+ab=0<_{β}^{α}$

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{4(a+b)\pm \sqrt{16(a+b)^{2}-48ab}}{2(12)}$

$=\frac{(a+b)\pm \sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-ab}}{6}$

Let $x=α=\frac{(a+b)+\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-ab}}{6}$

$β=\frac{(a+b)-\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-ab}}{6}$

Now, $12(x-α)(x-β)=0$

 
[IMG]
 

$\therefore$ x = $β$ $=\frac{a+b-\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-ab}}{6}$

text: If $y(x)=\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{1+\sin x}+\sqrt{1-\sin x}}{\sqrt{1+\sin x}-\sqrt{1-\sin x}}\right ),x\in \left (\frac{π}{2},π\right )$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x=\frac{5π}{6}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x\in \left (\dfrac{π}{2},π\right )$, $\dfrac{x}{2}\in \left (\dfrac{π}{4},\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$, so $\sin \dfrac{x}{2}>\cos \dfrac{x}{2}>0$.

Since $1\pm \sin x=\left (\cos \dfrac{x}{2}\pm \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right )^{2}$,

$\sqrt{1+\sin x}=\cos \dfrac{x}{2}+\sin \dfrac{x}{2},\sqrt{1-\sin x}=\left |\cos \dfrac{x}{2}-\sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right |=\sin \dfrac{x}{2}-\cos \dfrac{x}{2}$

The numerator becomes $2\sin \dfrac{x}{2}$ and the denominator $2\cos \dfrac{x}{2}$, so

$y=\cot ^{-1}\left (\tan \dfrac{x}{2}\right )=\cot ^{-1}\left (\cot \left (\dfrac{π}{2}-\dfrac{x}{2}\right )\right )=\dfrac{π}{2}-\dfrac{x}{2}$

because $\dfrac{π}{2}-\dfrac{x}{2}\in \left (0,\dfrac{π}{4}\right )$ lies in the principal range $(0,π)$ of $\cot ^{-1}$.

Therefore $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ throughout the interval, in particular at $x=\dfrac{5π}{6}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: If $\lim _{x\to \infty }\left (\sqrt{x^{2}-x+1}-ax\right )=b$, then the ordered pair (a, b) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For large $x$,

$\sqrt{x^{2}-x+1}-ax=x\left (\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}}-a\right )$

and the bracket tends to $1-a$. A finite limit therefore needs $a=1$; for $a=-1$ the expression is $\sqrt{x^{2}-x+1}+x\to \infty$.

With $a=1$, rationalising:

$\sqrt{x^{2}-x+1}-x=\frac{(x^{2}-x+1)-x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}-x+1}+x}=\frac{-1+\dfrac{1}{x}}{⎷1-\dfrac{1}{x}+\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}+1}\to \frac{-1}{1+1}=-\frac{1}{2}$

So $(a,b)=\left (1,-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9}. Then the number of elements in the set T = {A $\subseteq$ S : A $\neq$ $𝜙$ and the sum of all the elements of A is not a multiple of 3} is $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
3n type $\to$ 3, 6, 9 = P

3n $-$ 1 type $\to$ 2, 5 = Q

3n $-$ 2 type $\to$ 1, 4 = R

number of subset of S containing one element which are not divisible by 3 = ${}^{2}C_{1} +$ ${}^{2}C_{1} = 4$

number of subset of S containing two numbers whose some is not divisible by 3

= ${}^{3}C_{1}$ $\times$ ${}^{2}C_{1} +$ ${}^{3}C_{1}$ $\times$ ${}^{2}C_{1} +$ ${}^{2}C_{2} +$ ${}^{2}C_{2} = 14$

number of subsets containing 3 elements whose sum is not divisible by 3

= ${}^{3}C_{2}$ $\times$ ${}^{4}C_{1} + ({}^{2}C_{2}$ $\times$ ${}^{2}C_{1})2 +$ ${}^{3}C_{1}({}^{2}C_{2} +$ ${}^{2}C_{2}) = 22$

number of subsets containing 4 elements whose sum is not divisible by 3

= ${}^{3}C_{3}$ $\times$ ${}^{4}C_{1} +$ ${}^{3}C_{2}({}^{2}C_{2} +$ ${}^{2}C_{2}) + ({}^{3}C_{1}{}^{2}C_{1}$ $\times$ ${}^{2}C_{2})2$

= 4 + 6 + 12 = 22

number of subsets of S containing 5 elements whose sum is not divisible by 3.

= ${}^{3}C_{3}({}^{2}C_{2} +$ ${}^{2}C_{2}) + ({}^{3}C_{2}{}^{2}C_{1}$ $\times$ ${}^{2}C_{2})$ $\times$ 2 = 2 + 12 = 14

number of subsets of S containing 6 elements whose sum is not divisible by 3 = 4

$\Rightarrow$ Total subsets of Set A whose sum of digits is not divisible by 3 = 4 + 14 + 22 + 22 + 14 + 4 = 80.
